checks.finding: For amplitudes psi[a,z], rho[a,b]=sum_z psi[a,z]*conj(psi[b,z])=AA†; positive semidefinite, Hermitian, trace1. Environment sizes may differ across samplers.
Explicit complex-linear square matrix action plus norm preservation for every vector gives U†U=I by polarization; finite square dimension gives UU†=I.
The finite double sum equals Tr(D_S U rho U†)=Tr(P rho) with P=U†D_SU. The trace is real, matching the Real-valued definition.
Every orthogonal projector has an orthonormal image/kernel basis, giving an allowed U and Boolean accepts subset. Includes rank0/full rank and outputLength0.
Square modulus precedes the environment sum; no coherent cross-terms between distinct environment labels. Existing environment-sign-invariance theorem tests this.
For traceless Hermitian Delta=rho0-rho1, max_P |Tr(P Delta)|=sum_positive_eigenvalues=one_half*||Delta||_1, attained by the positive-eigenspace projector.
If trace distance equals2/3, the exact spectral projector witnesses the existential far condition. Arbitrary complex matrices are appropriate for distance, not a permitted sampler oracle.
All projectors have difference<=1/3 iff trace distance<=1/3, including equality.
Only fixed H,T,X,CNOT gates; distinct CNOT indices; zero initial state; Circuit.output does not affect run. Gate normalization is already formally proved.
One concrete finite-control transducer emits the entire family circuit on every input, with finite-polynomial runtime. No arbitrary length advice, density-matrix oracle, or distinguishability oracle.
Unary-delimited complete width/gate/index data are injective. For polynomial width w and gates g, length O(w+gw+g) stays polynomial.

Every total input maps into far-yes QSD(1/3,2/3). QSD membership and full/HV equivalence yield standard QSZK. Pad target description to length>=|x| so negligible target-size simulation error remains negligible in|x|.

If reference gate compilation is needed, state error<=1/96 each gives close<=17/48<3/8 and far>=31/48>5/8;3/8<(5/8)^2. Thus neither gate robustness nor strict polarization requires approximate attainment of the2/3 boundary.
Use standard QSD(1/8,7/8) completeness on the total language, then state error<=1/24 each. Resulting distances<=5/24 and>=19/24 strictly meet the required1/3 and2/3 thresholds.

Synthesize each of at mostM constant-arity gates to error1/(24*max(1,M)); telescoping and partial-trace contraction give state error<=1/24. T inverse is T^7; phase is irrelevant. Polynomial-size/time synthesis is only claimed gate by gate.

Relabel output wires first; append common zero output qubits to exact polynomial length; pad each environment and add the spare wire. Common output isometry preserves trace distance; discarded zeros change nothing.

The fixed reduction/compiler/padder/serializer has a polynomial-time implementation by the concrete finite-control transducer via standard deterministic simulation. This equivalence is not yet a Lean theorem.

verification.method: Read exact current source; independently derive formulas; check primary theorem statements and conventions; exact rational arithmetic for all displayed threshold margins.

rejected_misreadings: Comparing the full pure-state purifications instead of their mixed output states.
Coherently summing different environment amplitudes before taking squared modulus.
Treating the half trace norm as the unnormalized Schatten1 norm.
Claiming a supremum suffices for the existential far condition at exact2/3.
Restricting the mathematical distinguishing measurement to efficient H/T/CNOT circuits.
Reading the2002 honest-verifier result as the later full-QSZK theorem.
Using close-yes CQS statements without changing the polarity to far-yes QSD.
Compiling boundary-gap circuits without first leaving a quantitative margin.
Assuming negligible error in a possibly much shorter target instance is automatically negligible in the original input.
Claiming polynomial synthesis for an arbitrary many-qubit matrix rather than each constant-arity gate.
Allowing arbitrary polynomially bounded register-length functions to act as advice.
